categories.main_business_segments: Molina Healthcare operates four reportable segments: Medicaid, Medicare, Marketplace, and Other. The company is a pure-play government-sponsored healthcare provider serving approximately 5.0 million members across 20 states as of December 31, 2023. Medicaid represents the largest segment at 81% of consolidated premium revenue, followed by Medicare and Marketplace segments. The company arranges and pays for healthcare services for low-income families and individuals eligible for government-sponsored programs.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company utilizes managed care delivery models with emphasis on primary care coordination, utilization management, and population health management. Core operational methods include capitated and fee-for-service provider payment arrangements, claims processing systems, medical informatics for clinical decision-making, and outsourced pharmacy benefit management services through CVS Caremark. The company has invested in artificial intelligence administrative tools and initiatives to enhance operations and reduce costs, and employs evidence-based clinical policies for care management and quality improvement.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Primary customers are state Medicaid agencies and the federal government (CMS). The company serves low-income families, children, elderly, disabled, and dual-eligible individuals (Medicare-Medicaid). End markets include Medicaid programs (TANF, ABD, CHIP, Medicaid Expansion, LTSS), Medicare Advantage plans, and ACA Marketplace plans. The company operates in 20 states with significant concentration in California, New York, Texas, and Washington, which collectively represent approximately 51% of Medicaid premium revenue.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates across 20 states: Arizona, California, Florida, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Louisiana, Massachusetts, Michigan, Mississippi, Missouri, Nebraska, Nevada, New Mexico, New York, Ohio, South Carolina, Texas, and Washington. Major markets include California, New York, Texas, and Washington. The company has a significant presence in the Southwest, Midwest, and coastal regions of the United States.
categories.supply_chain_position: Molina Healthcare operates in the midstream of the healthcare supply chain as a managed care intermediary. The company contracts with providers (physicians, hospitals, ancillary providers, pharmacies) on one side and receives capitated payments from government agencies on the other side. The company arranges, pays for, and manages healthcare services, positioning itself between government payors and healthcare providers while bearing medical cost risk.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include organic growth through new state procurement opportunities and market share expansion, inorganic growth via accretive mergers and acquisitions, strong medical care ratio and G&A management for sustainable margins, and capital reinvestment or shareholder returns. The company targets 13-15% revenue growth through 2026. R&D initiatives focus on artificial intelligence for administrative efficiency, value-based contracting capabilities, clinical operations improvements, and enhanced operating models. The company emphasizes quality accreditation (NCQA), health equity, and long-term services and supports distinction.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through fixed monthly per-member per-month (PMPM) capitation payments from state Medicaid agencies and the federal government (CMS) for Medicare and Marketplace plans. Premium rates vary by state, line of business, demographics, and health risk factors. Additional revenue includes premium tax revenue, investment income, and service revenue from long-term services and supports consultative services. In 2023, premium revenue was $32.5 billion, representing 95.5% of total revenue of $34.1 billion.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors in Medicaid include Centene Corporation, CVS Health Corporation, Elevance Health, UnitedHealth Group, and large not-for-profit organizations. In Medicare, competitors include CVS Health, Humana, and UnitedHealth Group. In Marketplace, the primary competitor is Centene Corporation. Molina positions itself as a pure-play government-sponsored healthcare provider with industry-leading margins at approximately 5% pre-tax, a 75% new contract win rate, and 100% re-procurement win rate for Medicaid RFPs. The company emphasizes low-cost, high-quality service delivery.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: Molina is a FORTUNE 500 company with 2023 total revenue of $34.1 billion and net income of $1.1 billion. Premium revenue grew 5% year-over-year to $32.5 billion. The company achieved 20% revenue growth and 26% earnings per share growth from 2020 to 2023. Net income per diluted share was $18.77 in 2023 compared to $13.55 in 2022. The company serves 5.0 million members and has approximately 18,000 employees. After-tax margin improved to 3.2% in 2023 from 2.5% in 2022.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Molina differentiates itself as a low-cost, high-quality, reliable health plan focused exclusively on government-sponsored healthcare. Key value propositions include: singular focus enabling operational efficiencies, strong provider networks with cultural and linguistic competency, comprehensive care management and population health programs, quality accreditation and health equity recognition, seamless member experience across Medicaid-to-Marketplace transitions, and proven track record of RFP success. The company emphasizes appropriate access to care, preventive health services, and cost-effective medical management while maintaining industry-leading margins.
